newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bakun dam fully backed by Malaysia, PM says.
newsitem.headline: Bakun dam fully backed by Malaysia, PM says.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Tuesday he hoped investors in the $5.5 billion Bakun dam would be reassured by his government's support for the project.
While Malaysia has stopped short of providing the Bakun hydroelectric dam with a financial guarantee, Mahathir reiterated the project's importance to the country.

"...the government is fully committed to this project, regards it as a national project and we will always be behind this project," Mahathir said at the underwriting pact for the dam operating company's initial public offering (IPO).
The dam is being built in Sarawak state in Borneo island.

Talk in the Malaysian market in the past few months has suggested the listing of Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHEC) had drawn a lukewarm response from foreign investors, who along with Malaysians were allocated 25 percent of the IPO.

"I do hope that the people who are going to underwrite as well as to invest in this project feel comfortable with this assurance that the government will give this project every support," Mahathir told the signing ceremony.
BHEC is offering 375 million shares priced at two ringgit each through a consortium of 54 underwriters. The stock listing is expected to take place in late July or early August.
Asked by a reporter for his view on the performance of Bakun's IPO, Mahathir said it was hard to predict what the stock would do.
"Bakun is a sure thing, but it will take time (to warm up)," he said.
